title: Preserve committed NSX Policy steps after a later PowerShell failure
prompt:
Platform engineering applies a two-step NSX Policy firewall change from PowerShell. The source group PATCH can commit before the later security-policy PATCH fails, so the workflow must preserve and report the completed step instead of reducing the run to one generic exception.

Finish `VcfNsxPartialRollout/VcfNsxPartialRollout.psm1`. Before implementing, research the `PatchGroupForDomain` and `PatchSecurityPolicyForDomain` operations and their VMware VCF PowerCLI 9.1 generated bindings in official VMware sources. Confirm their request and response models, documented statuses, and error representation, and cite the source URLs consulted.

Keep the supplied manifest prerequisite on `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` version `13.5.0.25380678`; its official `VMware.OpenAPI` dependency loads the generated `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy` clients and models. Do not install, copy, generate, or vendor a VMware module, assembly, binding, SDK, or OpenAPI file. Production traffic must use the caller-supplied, already configured `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Api.PolicyApi` and `VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Api.DfwSecurityPolicyApi` instances. Both clients are caller-owned. Do not bypass them with `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `HttpClient`, curl, raw sockets, or another direct REST client.

Export exactly one function:

`Invoke-VcfNsxPartialRollout -PolicyApi <VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Api.PolicyApi> -DfwSecurityPolicyApi <VMware.Bindings.Nsx.Policy.Api.DfwSecurityPolicyApi> -DomainId <string> -GroupId <string> -SecurityPolicyId <string> -GroupDisplayName <string> -IpAddress <string[]> -PolicyDisplayName <string> -RuleDisplayName <string> -DestinationGroupPath <string> -PolicySequenceNumber <uint32> -RuleSequenceNumber <uint32> -ReportPath <string> [-GroupDescription <string>] [-PolicyDescription <string>] [-RuleNotes <string>]`

Requirements:

- Validate the complete call before invoking either operation. Required strings must not be blank. Display names are at most 255 characters. `IpAddress` contains 1 through 25,000 ordered, non-blank strings. `PolicySequenceNumber` is at most 999,999 and `RuleSequenceNumber` is at most 2,147,483,647. A bound group or policy description is non-blank and at most 1,024 characters; bound rule notes are non-blank and at most 2,048 characters.
- Build a fresh generated `Group` with exactly one generated `IPAddressExpression`. Set only `ResourceType`, `DisplayName`, and `Expression`, plus `Description` only when `GroupDescription` was explicitly bound. The expression sets only `ResourceType` and `IpAddresses`. Preserve address order.
- Build a fresh generated `SecurityPolicy` with one generated `Rule`. Set only `ResourceType`, `DisplayName`, `Category`=`Application`, `SequenceNumber`, `Stateful`=`true`, and `Rules`, plus `Description` only when `PolicyDescription` was explicitly bound. The rule sets only `ResourceType`, `DisplayName`, `SequenceNumber`, `SourceGroups`, `DestinationGroups`, `Services`, `Scope`, `Action`, and `Direction`, plus `Notes` only when explicitly bound. The source is `/infra/domains/<DomainId>/groups/<GroupId>` using the raw identifiers, the destination is the caller value, services and scope are each exactly `ANY`, action is `ALLOW`, and direction is `IN_OUT`.
- Unset optional, defaulted, and read-only model properties must remain genuinely unset so the generated serializer omits them. Do not substitute null, an empty string, an empty object, an empty array, false, zero, or an API default for an unset value.
- Invoke `PolicyApi.PatchGroupForDomain` first. Only after its documented 200 response succeeds may `DfwSecurityPolicyApi.PatchSecurityPolicyForDomain` run. Do not retry, roll back, or continue after a change HTTP failure. Each successful call is a separately committed step.
- A generated VMware `ApiException` representing an HTTP change failure is a workflow result, not a thrown terminal error. Stop and return a report. Preserve its HTTP status and, when its `ErrorContent` is or contains a valid documented `ApiError`, the top-level integral `error_code`. If the first operation fails, report only that failed step. Transport failures and local validation failures remain terminating errors and must not create a report.
- Return a report object with properties in this exact order: `Status`, `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Steps`. Each step has `Name`, `OperationId`, and `Status` in that order; a failed step then has `HttpStatus` and, only when present, `ErrorCode`. Status is `succeeded` when both operations commit, `failed` when the first fails, and `partial_failure` when the group commits and the policy fails.
- Write the same report atomically to `ReportPath` as compact UTF-8 JSON without a BOM followed by one LF. Create missing report parent directories. Never include either generated client, a credential, Authorization value, response body, generated exception text, or transport exception text in the report.

If `PatchGroupForDomain` commits and `PatchSecurityPolicyForDomain` returns a documented 503 `ApiError` with `error_code` 73001, return and write exactly one succeeded step followed by one failed step.

Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File tests/verify.ps1`. Do not modify the module manifest; edit only `VcfNsxPartialRollout/VcfNsxPartialRollout.psm1`.
scenario: the source-group PATCH commits, the later security-policy PATCH returns a documented 503 ApiError, and the PowerShell workflow must accurately preserve and report both outcomes
